intent: The i3blocks shutdown countdown shows and enforces minute-precision shutdown times (e.g. 18:30) now that /etc/shutdown-schedule.conf carries *_MINUTES keys, while still reading pre-migration hour-only files.
scope: Non-goal: the writers (screen-locker helper, digital-wellbeing installer) live in their own repos
changes: Parse MON_WED_MINUTES/THU_SUN_MINUTES/MORNING_END_MINUTES, prefer them, fall back to *_HOUR * 60; reject values outside 0-1440
Shutdown epoch and window thresholds computed from minutes; still builtins only (no forks)
Regression test: 18:30 minutes config shows '⏻ 18:30' at 18:15 and '⏻ SHUTDOWN' at 18:31 while the legacy HOUR copy says 18

verification.evidence: All i3blocks efficiency regression tests passed (fork count <= 1 for the countdown)

verification.command: SHUTDOWN_CONFIG=<dual|legacy fixture> NOW_EPOCH=<Tue 17:00/18:29/18:31, Thu 22:00> bash shutdown_countdown.sh

risks: A config with only *_MINUTES and malformed values shows INVALID TIME instead of a countdown (display only; enforcement is the check script)
rollback: git revert the commit; the old script reads the *_HOUR keys, which every writer still emits
Re-run the live block and confirm it shows the hour-rounded time
